bibl.title: CUT&Tag for efficient epigenomic profiling of small samples and single cells

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: where a given chromatin protein sits on the genome - a quantity with NO GROUND TRUTH, so that every method for measuring it can only be checked against another method for measuring it
span.quote: To determine if true CTCF binding sites could be distinguished from accessible features by read depth, we compared the CUT&Tag read count at high-confidence CTCF sites (defined by peak-calling on CUT&RUN data 18 ) to the CUT&Tag read count at accessible sites (defined by peak-calling on ATAC-seq data

span.label: whether tethering a Tn5 transposase to an antibody in intact cells can profile chromatin at high resolution from very few cells - and how you would know it had
span.quote: Chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing (ChIP-seq) and its variations 2 – 5 suffer from low signals, high backgrounds and epitope masking due to cross-linking, and low yields require large numbers of cells

span.label: CUT&Tag: antibody-tethered pA-Tn5 tagmentation in situ, giving sequencing-ready libraries in one tube in one day, down to 60 cells and into single cells
span.quote: All steps from live cells to sequencing-ready libraries can be performed in a single tube on the benchtop or a microwell in a high-throughput pipeline, and the entire procedure can be performed in one day.

span.label: method
span.quote: In CUT&Tag, a chromatin protein is bound in situ by a specific antibody, which then tethers a protein A-Tn5 transposase fusion protein. Activation of the transposase efficiently generates fragment libraries with high resolution and exceptionally low background.

span.label: chromatin state as a genome-wide pattern of protein occupancy that differs between cell types and is detectable in one cell at a time
span.quote: The aggregate of single cell chromatin profiling closely matched profiles generated in bulk samples (Fig. 6b ), with high correlations (Pearson’s r = 0.89, Supplementary Fig. 6b ). Individual cells were ranked by the genome-wide number of reads, and the unique fragments are displayed in tracks for each cell. Strikingly, the majority of reads from individual cells fall within H3K27me3 blocks defined in bulk profiling, indicating high recovery in single cell chromatin profiling

span.label: an antibody binds the target protein in permeabilised unfixed cells, a protein A-Tn5 fusion is tethered to it, excess is washed away, and Mg++ activates the transposase so that adapters integrate at the bound sites - one tube, no cross-linking
span.term: an antibody binds the target protein in permeabilised unfixed cells, a protein A-Tn5 fusion is tethered to it, excess is washed away, and Mg++ activates the transposase so that adapters integrate at the bound sites - one tube, no cross-linking
span.quote: In CUT&Tag, a chromatin protein is bound in situ by a specific antibody, which then tethers a protein A-Tn5 transposase fusion protein. Activation of the transposase efficiently generates fragment libraries with high resolution and exceptionally low background.

span.label: THE LOW BACKGROUND IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN STATISTICAL: the enzyme is tethered first and the excess washed away, and only THEN is it activated by Mg++. Nothing is cut until the antibody has already chosen the site
span.quote: We then activated the transposome by addition of Mg ++ , integrating adapters spanning sites of H3K27me3-containing nucleosomes

span.label: and ChIP works the other way round - fragment first, then select - which is what the paper blames for its noise: `the VAGARIES OF CROSSLINKING AND FRAGMENTING chromatin have limited chromatin profiling by ChIP-seq to AN ARTISAN TECHNIQUE`
span.quote: While ChIP-based methods have been extensively used in model cell line systems, the vagaries of crosslinking and fragmenting chromatin have limited chromatin profiling by ChIP-seq to an artisan technique where each experiment requires optimization.

span.label: and the residual background has a NAMED CAUSE with a testable signature: `some UN-TETHERED pA-Tn5 binding to exposed DNA in situ`. That is why accessible sites appear at all in a factor profile, and why read depth separates the two classes
span.quote: This probably results from some un-tethered pA-Tn5 binding to exposed DNA in situ, but it is straightforward to distinguish antibody-tethered sites from accessible sites by the vast difference in read coverage

span.label: THE COMPARISONS HAVE NO INDEPENDENT REFERENCE AND THE PAPER KEEPS CHANGING WHOSE OUTPUT IS THE TRUTH. `high-confidence CTCF sites (DEFINED BY PEAK-CALLING ON CUT&RUN DATA)` against `accessible sites (DEFINED BY PEAK-CALLING ON ATAC-SEQ DATA)` - both reference sets are another method's answer
span.quote: To determine if true CTCF binding sites could be distinguished from accessible features by read depth, we compared the CUT&Tag read count at high-confidence CTCF sites (defined by peak-calling on CUT&RUN data 18 ) to the CUT&Tag read count at accessible sites (defined by peak-calling on ATAC-seq data

span.label: and the choice of whose peaks changes the picture. In one figure each method is plotted on ITS OWN called peaks; in another all three are averaged at `the top 10,000 peaks detected by MACS2 IN CHIP-SEQ DATA`. Neither is wrong and they are not the same comparison
span.quote: Metaplot comparison of H3K4me1 histone modification signal in CUT&RUN, CUT&Tag, and ChIP-seq in K562 cells, averaged at the top 10,000 peaks detected by MACS2 in ChIP-seq data.

span.label: THE SINGLE-CELL RESULT IS SCORED AGAINST THE SAME METHOD RUN IN BULK: `narrow peaks were called using MACS2 ON BULK PROFILING DATA, and reads from scCUT&Tag were assigned to those peaks`. It measures internal consistency of CUT&Tag, which is the right thing to measure, and it is not external validation
span.quote: Fraction of reads in single K562 cells falling within called active peaks for the H3K4me2 histone modification using stringent criteria. Narrow peaks were called using MACS2 on bulk profiling data, and reads from scCUT&Tag were assigned to those peaks.

span.label: the spike-in control was SUBSTITUTED rather than performed: E. coli DNA carried over from transposase production was used `IN LIEU OF the heterologous spike-in DNA that is RECOMMENDED for CUT&RUN`. Its amount is a property of the enzyme prep, so it is a convenience standard and not a designed one - and the paper says which it is
span.quote: For standardization between experiments, we used the small amount of tracer genomic DNA derived from the E. coli during transposase protein production to normalize sample read counts in lieu of the heterologous spike-in DNA that is recommended for CUT&RUN

span.label: the transcription-factor result recovers only part of what it should: NPAT peak calling `generates a list of ~9000 sites`, which is `ONLY A FRACTION of the ~54,000 accessible sites`, and the remedy offered is to adjust the threshold - i.e. THE ANSWER MOVES WITH THE PEAK CALLER, which the paper states plainly
span.quote: Indeed, calling peaks by standard algorithms on NPAT CUT&Tag data generates a list of ~9000 sites that includes histone gene promoters and 10% of ATAC-defined accessible sites (Supplementary Fig. 4 ). While this is only a fraction of the ~54,000 accessible sites defined in K562 cells, adjusting the threshold and stringency of NPAT peak calling may improve detection.

span.label: resolution is BETTER than ChIP and WORSE than its own predecessor, and the paper reports the losing comparison: Tn5 protects 80 bp `LARGER THAN the ~45 bp protected from MNase in CUT&RUN`
span.quote: This shows that CUT&Tag protects a “footprint” spanning 80 bp directly over the CTCF motif (Fig. 5c ). While the segment protected from Tn5 integration is larger than the ~45 bp protected from MNase in CUT&RUN 9 , this indicates that the tethered transposase produces high resolution maps of factor binding sites.

span.label: and the wash stringency that removes untethered enzyme also costs signal: `300-500 mM salt concentrations resulted in somewhat REDUCED SIGNAL-TO-NOISE`. The knob that fixes the artefact degrades the measurement
span.quote: Similar footprints were obtained using different salt concentration washes, although 300–500 mM salt concentrations resulted in somewhat reduced signal-to-noise

span.label: PRO-seq was chosen as the validation reference SPECIFICALLY because it is `unrelated to chromatin profiling` and does not rely on annotations
span.note: eliminates: the circularity that every other comparison in the paper carries - an independent instrument agreeing is evidence in a way that another chromatin method agreeing is not · outcome: held
span.quote: To validate RNAPII CUT&Tag without relying upon annotations, which are typically based on mapping of processed transcripts, we chose transcriptional run-on data obtained with the base-pair-resolution PRO-seq technique, which provides direct mapping of RNAPII using a method that is unrelated to chromatin profiling

span.label: NPAT was chosen as a target BECAUSE its binding sites are already known - about 80, all in two histone-gene clusters
span.note: eliminates: the objection that a factor profile cannot be told from accessible chromatin: with a known answer, ~99% of read counts landed on the histone gene promoters · outcome: held
span.quote: We used an antibody to the NPAT nuclear factor, a transcriptional coactivator of the replication-dependent histone genes, in CUT&Tag reactions. NPAT binds only ~80 accessible sites in the histone clusters on chromosome 1 and chromosome 6 24 , thus we can compare true binding sites with accessible sites.

span.label: all three methods were downsampled to the same read depth - 8 million mapped reads - before any comparison
span.note: eliminates: sequencing depth as the explanation of the background difference · outcome: held
span.quote: To directly compare the three techniques, we set the read depth of each dataset to 8 million reads each. Landscapes for each of the three methods are similar, but background noise dominates in ChIP-seq datasets

span.label: an IgG antibody was used to measure integration with nothing to tether to
span.note: eliminates: untethered transposase as the source of the signal - though NOT entirely, since the paper later attributes real residual counts at accessible sites to `some un-tethered pA-Tn5 binding to exposed DNA in situ` · outcome: partial
span.quote: In contrast, incubation of cells with a non-specific IgG antibody, which measures untethered integration of adapters, produced very sparse landscapes

span.label: whether the CTCF sites separated by read depth are really CTCF sites, checked against SEQUENCE rather than against another assay
span.note: eliminates: the reference-circularity for this one result: the high-read class is enriched for CTCF motifs at E = 2.1e-69 and the low class is not. A MOTIF IS NOT A METHOD'S OUTPUT · outcome: held
span.quote: Based solely on read depth, we discriminate ~5600 CTCF bound sites with a 1% false discovery rate. Comparing motif enrichment in these two classes demonstrates that the high signals correspond to CTCF motifs ( E -value = 2.1 × 10 −69 ), and the low signals do not.

span.label: the spike-in normalisation recommended for CUT&RUN was replaced by carried-over E. coli DNA from the enzyme preparation
span.note: eliminates: nothing by design - it standardises between experiments, but its quantity is a property of the protein prep rather than a controlled addition, and the paper says it is used `in lieu of` the recommended control · outcome: partial
span.quote: For standardization between experiments, we used the small amount of tracer genomic DNA derived from the E. coli during transposase protein production to normalize sample read counts in lieu of the heterologous spike-in DNA that is recommended for CUT&RUN

span.quote: In CUT&Tag, a chromatin protein is bound in situ by a specific antibody, which then tethers a protein A-Tn5 transposase fusion protein. Activation of the transposase efficiently generates fragment libraries with high resolution and exceptionally low background.

While the segment protected from Tn5 integration is larger than the ~45 bp protected from MNase in CUT&RUN 9 , this indicates that the tethered transposase produces high resolution maps of factor binding sites.

span.label: `true binding sites` - AS OPERATIONALISED HERE, THE PEAK CALLS OF A DIFFERENT METHOD. CTCF truth is CUT&RUN's peak list; accessibility truth is ATAC-seq's. THE WORD `TRUE` IS DOING WORK THAT NO EXPERIMENT IN THIS PAPER DOES, and the paper is explicit about which method supplied each list
span.quote: To determine if true CTCF binding sites could be distinguished from accessible features by read depth, we compared the CUT&Tag read count at high-confidence CTCF sites (defined by peak-calling on CUT&RUN data 18 ) to the CUT&Tag read count at accessible sites (defined by peak-calling on ATAC-seq data

span.label: THE ONE PLACE `TRUE` IS EARNED, AND THE PAPER SAYS WHY IT CHOSE IT: PRO-seq, picked `to validate RNAPII CUT&Tag WITHOUT RELYING UPON ANNOTATIONS` because it `provides direct mapping of RNAPII USING A METHOD THAT IS UNRELATED TO CHROMATIN PROFILING`. The independence is the argument, and it is stated as the reason for the choice
span.quote: To validate RNAPII CUT&Tag without relying upon annotations, which are typically based on mapping of processed transcripts, we chose transcriptional run-on data obtained with the base-pair-resolution PRO-seq technique, which provides direct mapping of RNAPII using a method that is unrelated to chromatin profiling

span.label: the NPAT experiment is a genuine POSITIVE CONTROL - a target chosen because its answer is already known. `NPAT binds only ~80 accessible sites in the histone clusters ... THUS WE CAN COMPARE TRUE BINDING SITES WITH ACCESSIBLE SITES`. Picking the target for the sake of the control is the rare move
span.quote: We used an antibody to the NPAT nuclear factor, a transcriptional coactivator of the replication-dependent histone genes, in CUT&Tag reactions. NPAT binds only ~80 accessible sites in the histone clusters on chromosome 1 and chromosome 6 24 , thus we can compare true binding sites with accessible sites.

span.label: `signal-to-noise` - here it is THE FRACTION OF READS FALLING INSIDE CALLED PEAKS, at a fixed read depth. `Only CUT&Tag reaches a fraction of 0.6 within peaks` is therefore a statement about the method AND about whatever called the peaks
span.quote: We found that both CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag populate peaks more deeply than ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq, demonstrating that they have exceptionally low signal-to-noise (Fig. 3b ). In addition, CUT&Tag more rapidly populates peaks at low sequencing depths, where ~2 million reads are equivalent to 8 million for CUT&RUN (or 20 million for ChIP-seq), demonstrating the exceptionally high efficiency of CUT&Tag. Of all the methods, only CUT&Tag reaches a fraction of 0.6 within peaks.

span.label: and ATAC-seq is the counter-case that motivates the whole design: it maps accessible and factor-bound sites but `THE SPECIFIC CHROMATIN PROTEINS BOUND AT THESE SITES MUST BE INFERRED`. A method that sees WHERE but not WHO
span.quote: Although methods like ATAC-seq map accessible and factor-bound sites 17 , the specific chromatin proteins bound at these sites must be inferred from motif or chromatin profiling data.

span.label: extends → CUT&RUN - the same tethering strategy with the nuclease replaced by a transposase, which removes the separate library-preparation step
span.quote: This shows that CUT&Tag protects a “footprint” spanning 80 bp directly over the CTCF motif (Fig. 5c ). While the segment protected from Tn5 integration is larger than the ~45 bp protected from MNase in CUT&RUN 9 , this indicates that the tethered transposase produces high resolution maps of factor binding sites.

span.label: contradicts → ChIP-seq as a general-purpose chromatin profiling method - `the vagaries of crosslinking and fragmenting chromatin have limited chromatin profiling by ChIP-seq to AN ARTISAN TECHNIQUE where each experiment requires optimization`
span.quote: While ChIP-based methods have been extensively used in model cell line systems, the vagaries of crosslinking and fragmenting chromatin have limited chromatin profiling by ChIP-seq to an artisan technique where each experiment requires optimization.

span.label: supports → PRO-seq's map of engaged RNA polymerase II - the two agree, and the agreement counts BECAUSE the methods are unrelated
